## In brief - PLR launches opposition to the VAT increase for the 13th AVS pension - Standard rate: +0.4 percentage points, to 8.5% - The popular vote is scheduled for 29 November - The arguments were presented in Bern
## Key facts - Who → Swiss PLR - Subject → financing the 13th AVS pension through VAT - Increase → 0.4 percentage points, to 8.5% - Approval → in June by the Chambers - Deadline → popular vote on 29 November
Swiss PLR launched today, Monday, the campaign against the VAT increase intended to finance the 13th AVS pension. The party presented its arguments at a press conference in Bern.
The people will vote on the increase in the popular vote on 29 November. The issue put to a vote, according to the PLR's account, does not amount to a dispute over the payment of the 13th AVS pension. What is considered unacceptable is the method chosen to finance it.
### The contested increase
The target is the increase in the standard rate of 0.4 percentage points, to 8.5%, approved by the Chambers in June. PLR describes the increase as harmful to purchasing power and the economy. Its criticism therefore concerns the burden of the measure and the way in which it should support the financing of the benefit.
At the press conference, the party linked the additional burden to household budgets. According to the argument made in Bern, these budgets are already being put under severe strain by increases in health insurance premiums, rents and current expenses. The source does not indicate an individual amount or provide a simulation for individual categories.
PLR also disputes the adequacy of the financing. Co-president Susanne Vincenz-Stauffacher argues: «Less than half is financed by this poorly drafted proposal». For the party, therefore, the vote brings together criticism of the cost for households and criticism of the solution's ability to cover the financing of the 13th AVS pension. To delve further into the pension provision section, the reader can consult the guide on AVS e LPP.
The framework provided by the party therefore contains a political assessment on two fronts: the impact of the standard rate and the solution's ability to finance the benefit. The text attributes both assessments to PLR and presents no alternative calculation. The campaign remains focused on the choice of instrument, while the payment of the 13th AVS pension is not called into question. For the cross-border commuter following the debate, the practical key is to distinguish the payment of the 13th AVS pension from its financing. The source says that the former is not being called into question by the PLR; the campaign instead concerns the increase in VAT and the standard rate set at 8,5% after an increase of 0,4 percentage points.
This distinction prevents turning the vote into a decision described by the source as being in favor of or opposed to the 13th itself. The issue identified is the cost of the solution. The PLR links it to purchasing power and the economy, while regarding households it speaks of an additional burden that would weigh heavily on budgets already under pressure from health insurance premiums, rent and current expenses.
### The scope for those living across the border
For a cross-border commuter, the text does not make it possible to calculate a change in pay, net income or personal budget. It does not report individual amounts, consumption, wages or a breakdown of the burden among categories of people. Nor does it provide a separate impact for Canton Ticino.
To avoid conflating different issues, the source does not address the G permit, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates, INPS or double taxation. These references therefore cannot be used to attribute to the news a consequence that the text does not describe. The only concrete connection provided by the article is the general reference to household budgets and current expenses.
Also outside the text are the exact amount of the additional burden for a single household, any possible difference between personal circumstances and a numerical measure of overall coverage. The article does not provide these figures; therefore, the political position should be read as a campaign argument, not as a simulation of every reader's budget.
The assessment of whether the funding is sufficient must also be correctly attributed. It is not presented as a neutral fact or as an independent calculation: it is the judgment of the PLR, expressed by co-president Susanne Vincenz-Stauffacher, according to which less than half would be financed by the project. For the section on premiums cited in the source, an in-depth analysis is available at assicurazione malattia.

1. Identify the measure. This concerns the increase in VAT intended to finance the 13th AVS, not a dispute over its payment. 2. Establish the numerical figure. item.description: The Program Agreement between the Province of Como and the Municipality of Carlazzo finances a road of 1,242,383.84 euros, with 1,042,383.84 euros from the Municipality and 200,000 euros from the Province, to be built by 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Province of Como and Carlazzo sign the Program Agreement. - The new road costs 1.242.383,84 euros. - The route bypasses the historic center of Carlazzo. - Provincial funds will be disbursed during 2026.
## Key facts - Work → connection between Via per San Pietro and Via Provinciale - Location → former Carlazzo plant nursery area, along SP 10 - Total cost → 1.242.383,84 euros - Municipality funding → 1.042.383,84 euros - Province funding → 200.000 euros - Disbursement → during 2026 - Provincial contribution → 80% upon receipt of the executive project, 20% upon completion of the works - Management → Municipality as contracting authority; Province supervises
Province of Como and the Municipality of Carlazzo have signed a Program Agreement for the construction of the new connecting road between Via per San Pietro and Via Provinciale. The route is planned near the former plant nursery area, in the municipal territory of Carlazzo, along SP 10 della Val Cavargna.
The project has a total cost of 1.242.383,84 euros. The Municipality of Carlazzo will finance the project with 1.042.383,84 euros, while the Province of Como will contribute 200.000 euros. The funds come from their own budgets and will be disbursed during 2026.
### The connection and cross-border workers’ traffic
The new route will connect SP 10 della Val Cavargna with Via per San Pietro without passing through the historic center of Carlazzo. Today, that part of the town is affected by significant traffic, particularly due to the daily passage of cross-border workers. The road network is described as narrow, winding and unsuitable for the transit of medium-sized vehicles.
The President of the Province of Como, Fiorenzo Bongiasca, explained: «With this Program Agreement, the Province of Como confirms its commitment to the safety and efficiency of the provincial road network».
For those crossing the border for work, the concrete element of the agreement is the planned connection that will bypass the historic center. The text links the new road to easing traffic in the town, improving residents’ quality of life and facilitating the journeys of those who cross the border every day. No opening date, travel times or numerical estimate of the reduction in traffic are provided.
The road will also serve as access to the future development of sports facilities that the Municipality is developing precisely in the former plant nursery area. The Municipality will handle all technical and administrative activities, from design to final inspection, taking on the role of contracting authority. The Province will supervise the implementation of the project. The Mayor of Carlazzo, Piera Antonella Mazza, described the project as one that has been awaited for many years and is destined to benefit the historic center. ### What changes in the daily commute
To read the news from the cross-border worker's point of view, the comparison must be made between the road network described today and the function assigned to the new route. The source presents a road project designed to ease passage through the historic center and facilitate the travel of those who cross the border for work.
| Element | Situation described | Intended function | |---|---|---| | Historic center | Significant traffic also linked to cross-border workers | Connection without passing through it | | Road network | Narrow, winding and unsuitable for medium-sized vehicles | New connection between SP 10 and Via per San Pietro | | Former nursery area | Site of the future sports complex | Access to the future facilities |
The first expected effect is therefore a different distribution of traffic within the built-up area. For residents, the objective declared by the authorities is to ease traffic in the historic center. For the cross-border worker, the stated benefit is the possibility of having a connection between SP 10 of Val Cavargna and Via per San Pietro without passing through the heart of Carlazzo.
The difference remains tied to the construction of the project. The Program Agreement defines the connection, the funding and the administrative responsibilities, but the source does not provide an opening date, a work schedule, an estimate of the minutes saved or data on the number of vehicles that will be diverted away from the center. For this reason, the result can be described in terms of its intended function, not as an already measured reduction in traffic.
Access to the future sports facilities also broadens the usefulness of the route beyond the mere passage of cross-border workers. The road is in fact connected both to the road network of Val Cavargna and to the development of the former nursery area. Those who wish to supplement the news with a general overview of travel can consult storico del traffico e delle code ai valichi and mappa dei valichi, keeping these tools separate from the specific data on the Carlazzo project.
The concrete reference therefore remains local: a narrow and winding road in the historic center is being complemented by a new connection planned between SP 10 and Via per San Pietro. The source links this change to the daily lives of cross-border workers, without adding estimates on travel times, distances or schedules.

For the cross-border commuter who crosses the border every day, the procedure set out in the agreement makes it possible to follow the project's development through precise administrative steps. The Municipality of Carlazzo is the contracting authority and will handle all technical and administrative activities, from design to final acceptance. The Province of Como, on the other hand, will be responsible for overseeing implementation and paying its contribution in two installments.
1. Distinguish the agreement from the road that is already open. The text authorizes the construction of the link, but does not indicate a date for opening it to traffic. 2. Wait for the executive project approved by the Municipal Council. Upon receipt of this project, the Province will disburse 80% of its contribution. 3. Follow the construction phase. The Municipality remains responsible for the project's activities, while the Province oversees the implementation of the project. 4. Verify the completion of the works and approval of the final acceptance certificate. Only at the end of this step will the remaining 20% of the provincial contribution be disbursed. 5. Consider the route's final function. Once built, the link will connect the SP 10 of Val Cavargna with Via per San Pietro without passing through the historic center, and will also serve the area of the future sports facilities.
This sequence helps to correctly interpret future updates. Approval of the executive project is the first financial milestone indicated by the source; completion of the works and final acceptance represent the final one. Until those steps have been completed, it is not possible to associate a usage date or a quantitative effect on cross-border commuter traffic with the project.

LUGANO – Nighttime work related to resurfacing the bridge over the Cassarate is scheduled on via alla Bozzoreda. The Department of Territory announced this, indicating that the work will take place between Monday 5 and Saturday 10 October.
The operations will begin at 20 and take place overnight. The construction site on the bridge over the Cassarate presents two distinct effects, both related to the operations taking place during the night. On the one hand, there are the noises produced by the machinery and equipment necessary for rehabilitating the road surface; on the other, the possibility of delays for motorists travelling along via alla Bozzoreda or the connecting roads.
The Department of Territory reports that the works were scheduled for nighttime specifically to contain disruption to traffic. This choice does not, however, eliminate the effects on public quiet. The equipment used for the works will generate noise and may therefore cause temporary disturbances in the area concerned.
As regards traffic, the notice speaks of delays of a few minutes. The forecast concerns via alla Bozzoreda and the connections with via Sonvico, via Ceresio, via Ciani and via Maraini. These are the roads mentioned in the communication and represent the road connections within which motorists may encounter slowdowns during the operations.

The main road affected is via alla Bozzoreda, in Lugano, as part of the rehabilitation of the road surface of the bridge over the Cassarate. The list of connecting roads includes via Sonvico, via Ceresio, via Ciani and via Maraini.
The general period, from lunedì 5 to sabato 10 ottobre, and the start time, set at 20, remain defined. The picture communicated is one of noise, disturbances to public quiet and possible delays limited to the roads indicated. ## What happens between 5 and 10 October
Between Monday 5 and Saturday 10 October, the bridge over the Cassarate will be affected by night-time works to refurbish the road surface. The operations will begin at 20 and take place overnight, according to the schedule communicated by the Department of the Territory.
For traffic, the expected effect is the possibility of delays of a few minutes. The notice concerns via alla Bozzoreda and the connecting roads: via Sonvico, via Ceresio, via Ciani and via Maraini. Drivers may therefore experience temporary slowdowns on the roads affected by the worksite.
Public quiet will also be affected during the working hours. The refurbishment will require the use of machinery and equipment that will generate noise. This is a temporary inconvenience linked to the night-time phase of the work, while scheduling it after 20 was chosen to limit the effects on traffic.
### The work schedule
The published schedule sets the work period between Monday 5 and Saturday 10 October and indicates 20 as the start time for the operations. The location affected is via alla Bozzoreda, in Lugano, as part of the refurbishment of the road surface of the bridge over the Cassarate.
During the indicated nights, the reported effects are therefore two: noise and disturbances to public quiet caused by the equipment, as well as possible delays of a few minutes along via alla Bozzoreda and on the connecting roads.

item.title: Hotels and restaurants: minimum wages +0.6% in 2027
item.description: In the hotel and restaurant industry, minimum wages will rise by 0,6% in 2027: for Category II, from 4'070 to 4'094 gross francs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Sector minimum wages: +0.6% in 2027 - The increase corresponds to expected inflation - Cat. II: from 4'070 to 4'094 gross francs - The summer season will begin on 1 May 2027
## Key facts - Sectors → hospitality and catering - Increase → 0.6% - Category → Cat. II - Gross monthly salary → from 4'070 to 4'094 francs - Forecasts → SECO inflation - End of winter season → 30 April 2027 - Start of summer season → 1 May 2027
The minimum wage in the hospitality and catering sector will increase by 0.6% in 2027. The decision was set by the sector’s social partners and corresponds to expected inflation, according to a joint statement issued in Basel.
The agreement was communicated by the employer organisations GastroSuisse, HotellerieSuisse and Swiss Catering Association, together with the worker representatives Hotel & Gastro Union, Syna and Unia. The adjustment concerns the sector’s minimum wages and stems from a mechanism that the employer organisations and trade unions had already agreed on last year.
The decision is based on the inflation forecasts of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, identified in the source by the acronym SECO. The increase is therefore presented by the social partners as an adjustment to the expected inflation for 2027.
### The decision of the social partners
For an employee holding a federal certificate of practical training or an equivalent qualification, i.e. Cat. II, the gross monthly salary will rise from 4'070 to 4'094 francs. The change therefore concerns a minimum level expressed in gross monthly francs and is not described in the source as a general change to all wages in the sector.
The move from 4'070 to 4'094 francs is the only quantified wage level in the statement. The statement identifies the profile through the federal certificate of practical training or the equivalent qualification and lists the amounts as gross monthly salary.
In the statement, the parties specify that this agreement allows them to «focus on negotiations concerning the new collective labour agreement». ## The mechanism already agreed
The increase announced for 2027 does not stem from negotiations started from scratch. The employers' organizations and the sector's trade unions had already agreed last year on the mechanism used to determine the adjustment. The decision now communicated therefore applies a criterion already shared by the social partners.
The parameter referred to is the expected rise in prices. SECO's inflation forecasts form the basis on which 0.6% was set for the minimum wages in the hotel and catering sector. The source does not attribute the announcement to a single person: it presents it as a joint position of the employers' associations and workers' representatives.
On one side are GastroSuisse, HotellerieSuisse and Swiss Catering Association. On the other are Hotel & Gastro Union, Syna and Unia. These are the organizations listed in the joint statement accompanying the agreement and that indicated the correspondence between the increase and the expected rise in prices.
### The effect on Cat. II
The most concrete point concerns Cat. II. The reference is to an employee with a federal certificate of practical training or an equivalent qualification. For this profile, the gross monthly amount rises from 4'070 to 4'094 francs. The difference reported by the source is therefore between two gross monthly amounts, while the percentage set by the social partners is 0.6%.
The agreement is not presented merely as a numerical update. In the statement, the parties explain that defining the minimum wages makes it possible to focus their efforts on negotiations concerning the new collective employment agreement. The source does not indicate the outcome of those negotiations and does not provide any other amounts for categories other than Cat. II.
The picture described therefore remains limited to the announced data: a mechanism already agreed, an inflation forecast from SECO and the adjustment of the minimum wage planned for 2027. ## When the seasonal increases will take effect
For seasonal contracts, the increase in minimum wages will not come into force through one single, undifferentiated date. The joint note indicates that the increases will be applied at the beginning of the summer season.
The timeline reported by the social partners is precise: the winter season ends no later than 30 April 2027. The summer season begins the following day, on 1 May 2027. For seasonal contracts, therefore, the start of the summer season marks the entry into force of the minimum wage increases.
### The succession of the seasons
The calendar indicated in the statement directly links the end of the winter season to the beginning of the summer season. 30 April 2027 represents the latest date indicated for the winter season; 1 May 2027 is the start date of the summer season. The source does not add any further dates or conditions for applying the increase.
The follow-up to the agreement also concerns the new collective labour agreement. Defining the increase allows the social partners to focus on the related negotiations, but the statement does not anticipate its contents, deadlines or results. Nor does it indicate any other seasonal periods beyond those linked to the end of winter and the start of summer.
The next step explicitly mentioned is therefore twofold: for seasonal contracts, applying the increases at the beginning of the summer season; for the signatory organizations, continuing negotiations on the new collective labour agreement. The dates communicated for the seasonal calendar remain 30 April 2027 and 1 May 2027.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/economia/1953120/salari-hotel-lavoro-meccanismo-datori)*

item.title: Tax credit for Ticino expenses: idea Giovani Centro
item.description: Up to 5% of salary, capped at 5.000 francs, 25% credit on spending; simulation of 170.000 workers leads to 850 million in additional spending and 212,5 million in public costs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Giovani del Centro propose a credit for spending in Ticino. - The share reaches 5% of salary, with a cap of 5 thousand francs. - The proposed credit is 25% of the spending incurred. - With 100% of Ticino workers, spending: 850 million francs.
## Key facts | Item | Value | |---|---| | Proponents | Giovani del Centro | | Share | Up to 5% of salary or self-employment income | | Maximum cap | 5 thousand francs | | Tax credit | 25% of spending | | Simulated participation | 100% of Ticino workers | | Estimated workers | Around 170 thousand | | Additional spending | 850 million francs | | Estimated public cost | Around 212,5 million francs |
Up to 5% of salary, with a cap of 5 thousand francs, to be allocated to purchases from local businesses participating in the initiative. This is the proposal presented in Ticino by Giovani del Centro through a generic parliamentary initiative: anyone who participated would receive a tax benefit calculated on the amount spent in Ticino.
### A measure to bring spending back to the canton
The plan has a dual purpose. On the one hand, it aims to support families and the middle class. On the other, it seeks to prevent spending from ending up outside the canton or abroad, directing it toward Ticino businesses. The mechanism connects consumers, who receive a discount on their taxes, with local merchants and small and medium-sized enterprises, which can count on new revenue.
In the example outlined by the proponents, a worker with a gross annual salary of 50 thousand francs would allocate 2.500 francs to the Ticino system. The sum would be spent at local businesses participating in the initiative. In exchange, the consumer would receive a tax credit of 25%, equal to 625 francs. The calcolatore fiscale may help keep the salary figure and that of the proposal separate, without turning the example into a rule that is already applicable.
The Giovani del Centro simulation then considers a scenario of full participation. With 100% of Ticino workers, estimated at around 170 thousand people, the canton's economy would record additional spending of 850 million francs. The overall cost to public coffers, in the form of reimbursed tax credits, would be around 212,5 million francs. This is the scenario indicated by the proponents, not an outcome already secured.
For a cross-border worker, however, the practical link remains to be defined. The text refers to every employee and provides the same rule for the income of self-employed workers, but does not specify the position of those using a G permit. Nor does it clarify whether or how the credit would relate to withholding tax, AVS, LPP, LAMal, reimbursements or double taxation. The initiative is generic and leaves the definition of the technical details and the assessment of its economic sustainability for the State to further analysis.
The president of Giovani del Centro, Giovanna Pedroni, and vice president Luca Taglialatela stressed that the assessment will be up to the competent offices of the Council of State. ...

1. Consider the text for what it is: a generic parliamentary initiative. It is not presented as an already operational mechanism; the technical details and sustainability still need to be examined in greater depth.
2. Identify one's starting point: employee or self-employed. The source provides for employees a share of up to 5% of salary and indicates the same rule for self-employed income. It does not add other categories or requirements.
3. Keep the calculations separate. The published reference is the gross annual salary of 50 thousand francs, with 2,500 francs allocated to spending and 625 francs in credit. simulatore busta paga can be used to read the gross figure, while the proposal remains a simulation and not an applicable provision.
4. Await the institutional step. The competent offices of the Council of State must assess financial sustainability; subsequent in-depth work will have to define the technical details. Only at that point can the reader verify which expenses and which businesses fall within the measure, based on the rules made available.
For a cross-border worker, operational caution is even simpler: do not attribute to the proposal an already-defined effect on one's tax or administrative position. The text indicates neither a deadline nor an office to which to send documents, so there is no documentary procedure to follow based on the source alone. The only concrete step already indicated is assessment by the competent offices.
The comparison with stores must also remain faithful to the proposal. The incentive concerns businesses in the area that participate, but no sectors, minimum amounts, or methods of proving expenditure are indicated. Presenting the credit as a guaranteed reimbursement would mean going beyond the content of the initiative.

item.title: Health insurers in Ticino: changing several times pays off
item.description: The Axa analysis reveals 563 francs of savings at the first exchange rate of the health insurance fund and 633 in Ticino: comparison between subsequent exchange rates, age and Swiss cantons.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - First switch: 563 average annual francs - Subsequent switches: 383 average annual francs - Ticino: 633 annual francs on the first switch - Analysis published before the 2027 premiums
## Key facts - Source → Axa analysis - Period observed → last four years - Customers considered → Axa customers with supplementary insurance - Subject → switches of basic insurance - Limitation → Axa does not offer basic insurance
563 francs a year: that is the average saving obtained by policyholders on their first switch of basic insurance in the analysis published by Axa shortly before the announcement of the new premiums for 2027. When the switch occurred again, the average saving was instead 383 francs a year.
The result puts into perspective the idea that the first switch exhausts the possible savings. The analysis takes into account all switches of basic insurance made over the last four years by Axa customers holding supplementary insurance.
> “Many policyholders assume that after a first switch there is hardly any savings potential left,” said Alexandra Gmür, head of healthcare provision at Axa.
### Cantons with the greatest margin
The potential was particularly high in cantons with high premiums. On the first switch, Geneva recorded average annual savings of 697 francs. It was followed by the Canton of Ticino with 633 francs, the Canton of Vaud with 594, Zurich with 588 and Basel-City with 554.
In Ticino, the savings obtained on the first switch were 31% higher than those from subsequent switches. The research also identifies differences based on age, but the central figure remains the comparison between the first switch and those made subsequently.
For the cross-border worker who works in the Canton of Ticino, the news remains limited to health insurance. The source refers to policyholders and Axa customers, but does not identify permit G, LAMal, AVS, LPP, withholding tax, INPS or double taxation and does not offer separate statistics on cross-border workers. To avoid attributing data that the research does not contain to it, confronto LAMal/CMI must be kept separate from the figures in the analysis. ## The second switch retains a margin
The figure of 383 francs per year helps interpret the second switch without turning it into a nil result. The analysis compares an average initial saving of 563 francs with a subsequent average saving of 383: the average advantage changes, but does not disappear. For those who assess new offers every year, the benefit therefore does not end after the first choice.
In the Canton of Ticino, the first switch produced an average of 633 francs, the highest figure among the cantons indicated after Geneva. The number does not amount to an automatic personal saving: it is an average derived from the assessment of the switches made by the Axa customers considered in the analysis. The figure should therefore be read as a reference for comparison, not as a guaranteed result for every policyholder.
### Differences between age groups
The group with the greatest average saving is that of 26-30-year-olds, at 451 francs per year. Those aged 19-25 stood at 436 francs. For policyholders over 51, the average potential was 417 francs, while for children and young people up to 18 years old it was 235 francs.
These figures show that age group factors into the interpretation of average savings. However, they do not replace a concrete comparison between the available offers, because the source does not link each figure to a single policy or individual choice.
### Models and deductibles
Axa recommends comparing premiums every year while also assessing alternative insurance models and deductibles. For a cross-border worker, the useful point is therefore the possibility of periodically reopening the comparison concerning the healthcare component, without confusing it with AVS, LPP, withholding tax or other sections of the cross-border employment relationship. The research does not quantify specific effects for those holding a G permit. The confronto dell'assicurazione sanitaria LAMal/CMI may remain the separate tool for this verification.

The recommendation from the analysis is simple: compare premiums every year, including alternative insurance models and deductibles. The data makes it possible to conduct an orderly review, but does not indicate an administrative procedure, deadline or specific document.
### 1. Start with basic insurance
The first filter is to keep the comparison within the same area analyzed by Axa: changes to basic insurance. Supplementary insurance forms part of the profile of the customers observed, but is not the subject of the reported savings. Separating the two levels prevents results relating to something else from being attributed to basic premiums.
### 2. Distinguish the first change from subsequent ones
Note whether the assessment concerns the first change or a subsequent change. The average indicated by the source is 563 francs per year in the first case and 383 francs in subsequent changes. Comparing these two reference points helps clarify what type of result is being observed.
### 3. Compare models and deductibles
The Axa recommendation also includes alternative insurance models and deductibles. These are therefore the parameters to include in the annual review together with the premium, without replacing data from one's own situation with a general average.
### 4. Read the result within the correct scope
The analysis was carried out on Axa customers holding supplementary insurance, while Axa does not offer basic insurance. For a cross-border worker, this means using the figures as guidance on the topic of health insurance, while keeping permit G, INPS, rebates and double taxation separate. item.title: Mastini Varese towards Fassa: look for first points in the championship
item.description: On Saturday 26 September at 18:30, Mastini Varese face Fassa after losing their opening game 2-4 to Pirati di Appiano; the team is looking to get off the mark in the standings.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Mastini beaten 2-4 by the Pirati di Appiano - Saturday 26 settembre at 18,30 away game in Fassa - Fassa beat Pergine 3-6 away - The away game in Caldaro is scheduled for 1° ottobre
## Key facts - Debut → Mastini Varese-Pirati di Appiano 2-4 - Next game → Fassa-Mastini, Saturday 26 settembre, at 18,30 - Rich's style → tactical precision and competitive intensity - Squad → still incomplete - Next stop → Caldaro, 1° ottobre
On Saturday 26 settembre at 18,30, Mastini Varese face the second matchday of the championship away in Fassa. The yellow-and-black team visit the highly rated Falcons with one clear objective: to sustain a high tempo for longer and try to earn points.
The matchup comes after the debut against the Pirati di Appiano, which ended 2-4. The defeat was not decisive: one of the goals came into an empty net, while analysis of the game left a positive assessment of the way Mastini performed on the ice. Rich's hockey is described as enjoyable, built on the balance between tactical precision and competitive intensity.
### The test against Fassa
However, the result against Appiano also highlighted a limitation. The volume of play generated by Mastini uses up a lot of energy; when the collective effort drops, the defensive structure becomes more vulnerable and allows penetrations and shots.
The statistics reinforce this reading. Against the Pirati, the Varese net received more than twice as many shots as the opponents. The defense was asked to do extra work in closing down, especially in the third period, when the fuel seemed to be running low. The trip to Fassa will therefore be a test to understand how long the team will be able to sustain its intensity.
Fassa come from an away win of 3-6 over Pergine, achieved without too many problems. The game promises to be different from the one against Appiano: the Pirati were described as more well-organized and predictable, while the Fassa side offer a less rigid and more varied game.
The composition of the squad also remains an element to watch. The awaited return of Tommaso Terzago, the addition of the long-absent Levi Glasman and the hope of an additional defenseman could provide the fuel needed to make the yellow-and-black team's drive more progressive and consistent. The source specifies, however, that these considerations come after only sixty minutes of play and are therefore partial. After Fassa, the schedule takes Mastini to Caldaro on 1° ottobre, for a tricky away game that on paper is almost impossible. ## Rhythm, energy and defense

Over 20mila toys intended for children, more than 300 electrical devices and about 300 textile products were seized during inspections carried out in recent days by the Guardia di Finanza of Varese at various commercial establishments in Busto Arsizio and Saronno. The tally also includes three merchants sanctioned and two reported for commercial fraud.
### The inspections and seizures
The Busto Arsizio Group and the Saronno Company operated as part of the provincial inspection effort against the sale of non-compliant and potentially dangerous products. Irregularities emerged in goods displayed for sale in three stores.

item.title: Dumenza, three home burglaries and one failed attempt
item.description: Three homes targeted in Dumenza on the evening of Friday, September 25: cash, gold and money stolen. A fourth attempt failed.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Three thefts committed in Dumenza in a single evening - Via Santuario, via Fiume and via Dante targeted - 600 euros, gold and other money stolen - A fourth break-in failed on via XX Settembre
## Key facts - When → Friday 25 September - Where → Dumenza - Completed thefts → three - Failed attempts → one - Money stolen → 600 euros on via Santuario - Streets affected → via Santuario, via Fiume, via Dante and via XX Settembre - Investigations → Carabinieri of the Dumenza Station
### The four incidents
Three home burglaries successfully carried out and a fourth failed attempt over the course of a single evening. This is the sequence recorded in Dumenza on Friday 25 September, where several homes were targeted by unknown perpetrators.
On via Santuario, the thieves managed to enter a home and took 600 euros in cash. Another theft was reported on via Fiume: in this case too, the criminals managed to enter a house and, after searching for valuables, took gold.
A third theft was committed in a home on via Dante. In this case, the haul consisted of gold and money, taken before the perpetrators managed to get away and disappear without a trace.
The situation was different on via XX Settembre. The unknown individuals heard the owners inside the home and decided to flee. The theft was not completed, but in this incident too the perpetrators managed to disappear without a trace.
The incidents affected four streets in the small municipality north of Varese. In three homes the theft was completed, while in the fourth case the attempt was interrupted after the owners were heard inside the house. The people concerned reported the incidents to the Carabinieri of the Dumenza Station. ## The targeted homes
The reconstruction of the cases begins on via Santuario, where the reported haul was 600 euros in cash. On via Fiume, by contrast, the perpetrators searched for valuables inside the home and took gold.
The third incident, on via Dante, involved a haul consisting of gold and money. The perpetrators managed to get away after taking whatever they found in the home, disappearing without a trace. On via XX Settembre, the outcome was different: the presence of the owners prompted the unknown individuals to flee before the theft could be completed.
### Hauls and outcomes
| Street | Outcome | Haul or circumstances | |---|---|---| | via Santuario | Completed theft | 600 euros in cash | | via Fiume | Completed theft | Gold | | via Dante | Completed theft | Gold and money | | via XX Settembre | Failed attempt | The owners were at home |
The string of incidents is described as unfortunately record-breaking for the small municipality. The figure concerns the concentration of the incidents: three completed thefts and a fourth attempted break-in on the same evening. The homes are located on different streets, but all within the territory of Dumenza.
The evening thus resulted in four reports with two distinct outcomes. On the one hand, the thieves managed to enter three homes and steal cash, gold, or both. On the other, the attempt on via XX Settembre ended when the unknown individuals heard the residents. After fleeing, the perpetrators of the three completed thefts also disappeared without a trace.
The available information links the individual incidents to their respective addresses: via Santuario for the 600 euros, via Fiume for the gold, via Dante for gold and money, via XX Settembre for the failed attempt. The Dumenza Carabinieri Station is now focusing its investigations on this sequence. ## The Carabinieri investigation
Following reports from the people concerned, the Carabinieri of the Dumenza Station are carrying out investigations to reconstruct what happened and try to identify those responsible for the thefts.
The investigators' work concerns the sequence recorded on the evening of Friday 25 September, with three completed thefts and a fourth attempt that was not carried through. The checks concern the homes indicated on Via Santuario, Via Fiume, Via Dante and Via XX Settembre, where the incidents described occurred.
For the failed break-in, the reported circumstance is the presence of the owners inside the house. After hearing them, the unknown individuals decided to flee. In the other three cases, however, the perpetrators managed to enter the homes, take the items mentioned and leave without a trace.
### The request to residents
The appeal to the public is to report to the Carabinieri any suspicious people or cars noticed on Friday evening in the areas concerned. The request concerns not only the streets where the homes were targeted, but more generally the territory of Dumenza.
Any detail could prove useful to the investigation. For this reason, both observations possibly made in the areas of Via Santuario, Via Fiume, Via Dante and Via XX Settembre, and those collected in other areas of the municipality on the same evening, are being recalled.
Residents' reports add to those already submitted by the people affected by the thefts. The investigations by the Carabinieri of the local Station will reconstruct what happened and try to identify those responsible for the sequence of incidents recorded in Dumenza.

item.title: Como, jewelry store robbery: two more arrests
item.description: A 32-year-old resident of Switzerland and a 25-year-old from the province of Monza arrested for the 90mila euro robbery at Stroili in Tavernola.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Two arrests for the robbery at the Stroili store in Tavernola - The heist yielded gold worth approximately 90mila euro - The two arrested individuals reside in Switzerland and the Monza area - The robbery was committed on 24 aprile
## Key facts - Operation: two arrests - Location: Stroili jewelry store in the Bennet in Tavernola - Loot: gold jewelry worth approximately 90mila euro - Date of the robbery: 24 aprile - Suspects arrested: a 32-year-old and a 25-year-old - Authorities: Como State Police and the Public Prosecutor’s Office
### The latest operation
On 25 settembre, the Como State Police arrested two Italian nationals as part of the investigation into the robbery at the Stroili jewelry store inside the Bennet in Tavernola. The operation was coordinated by the Public Prosecutor’s Office and carried out pursuant to a pretrial detention order issued by the GIP of Como.
They are a 32-year-old resident of Switzerland and a 25-year-old resident of the province of Monza. According to the evidence gathered during the investigation, the two are believed to have been involved in the heist committed on 24 aprile, when four people with their faces covered reached the shopping center in a rental car.
The robbery took place within a few minutes. While one of the group waited in the car, the others entered the jewelry store armed with a pistol and with their faces concealed by balaclavas. They threatened the employees and smashed the glass display cases with hammers, taking numerous gold jewelry items.
The total value of the stolen jewelry was estimated at approximately 90mila euro. Due to its manner and speed, the action was described as resembling a scene from a Hollywood action film. ## The investigation into the gang
### The previous arrests
The arrests on September 25 represent a new stage in the investigative activity launched after the assault on the Bennet jewelry store in Tavernola. The Como Mobile Squad reconstructed the participants’ roles and gathered evidence considered significant against all those involved in the robbery.
The investigation also concerns the mastermind behind the heist. The source reports that the most recent operation forms part of a broader context, in which the other three members of the gang had already been arrested in April and May 2026. The robbery had been committed by four individuals, with tasks divided between those waiting outside and those entering the store.
During the investigations following the arrests, searches were carried out. Those activities also uncovered part of the stolen goods, before they could be fenced. The recovered jewelry was returned to the Stroili jewelry store, which had been targeted in the assault.
The reconstruction includes several details described by investigators: the rental car used to reach Bennet, the covered faces, the gun shown to the employees, and the hammers used to smash the display cases’ glass. The haul consisted of numerous gold jewelry items, taken within a matter of minutes.
The Mobile Squad’s work focused both on the actual execution of the robbery and on identifying the participants and the alleged mastermind. The previous arrests and searches added details to the reconstruction of the heist and enabled some of the jewelry to be recovered. ## What happens now
### The procedural phase
After notification of the pretrial detention order, the two men arrested on 25 September were taken to the Como Prison. Their position remains linked to the investigation records and the evidence gathered by the Como State Police, coordinated by the Public Prosecutor’s Office.
The next step indicated by the source is the confirmation in court of the evidence that emerged during the investigations. The arrests were carried out on the basis of the order issued by the GIP of Como, while the strength of the evidence gathered will have to be verified in the proceedings.
From an investigative standpoint, the most recent operation fits into a sequence that had already led to the arrest of the other three members of the gang in the months of April and May 2026. The searches had also made it possible to recover some of the jewelry stolen from Stroili and return it to the store.
The matter remains focused on the proceedings relating to the robbery on 24 April at Bennet in Tavernola. The elements cited include the haul of approximately 90mila euro, the involvement of four individuals with different roles, the use of a rental car and the action carried out with a pistol, balaclava and hammers.
For the two arrested men, the next stage will therefore be the procedural one, identified in the records as the venue for confirmation of the investigative evidence. Until that stage, the reconstruction remains the one that emerged from the work of the State Police, the Como Mobile Squad and the Public Prosecutor’s Office.

item.description: Mps deputies seek clarification on the early withdrawal of 700,000 francs and the pension calculation for the resigning minister
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- Sergi and Pronzini ask for clarifications about Zali's pension entitlement - The order dismissing the case is dated 6 marzo 2019 - The advance withdrawal indicated is approximately 700mila franchi - The questions concern calculation, reduction and insurance period
- Main figures → Giuseppe Sergi and Matteo Pronzini, Mps deputies - Subject → Claudio Zali's pension case - Decision → order signed by Attorney General Andrea Pagani - Withdrawal → approximately 700mila franchi - Effective date → pension entitlement starting on 1° ottobre - Reform → parliamentary amendment during 2020
### The interpellation reopens an issue already discussed
Claudio Zali's departure from the Council of State of the Canton of Ticino prompted Giuseppe Sergi and Matteo Pronzini, Mps deputies, to submit an interpellation to the government. The two are asking for clarifications about the pension entitlement of the Lega minister who resigned and argue that his pension case is still far from clear. The issue had already emerged in 2018, after Pronzini's reports.
The reports led, in March of the following year, to an order dismissing the case signed by Attorney General Andrea Pagani with regard to Zali. The measure concerned the advance withdrawal intended to finance his primary residence, requested and obtained by the State Councillor in March 2016. The date indicated for the order is 6 marzo 2019.
### The move from the Court of Appeal to the government
Sergi and Pronzini start from that order. According to the interpellation, when Zali moved from the Court of Appeal to the Council of State, the occupational pension contributions were taken in by the Canton of Ticino, as provided for by the cited law. In return, the years spent in the service of the State as a teacher and magistrate would have been counted as years of service on the Council of State to determine the pension entitlement upon leaving the government.
The two parliamentarians' reading is that Zali had been entitled to the maximum pension entitlement from day one without paying a franc in pension contributions. They link this situation to the former pension rules for State Councillors, which they describe as still valid for the majority of the members of the current Executive.
The administrative chronology includes further steps. On 28 settembre 2015, an internal opinion from Ipct, sent by email to the entire Council of State by the then deputy director, indicated that the advance withdrawal would have an impact on the future pension entitlement. On 27 novembre 2015, Zali forwarded to Ipct the application for an advance withdrawal, a pledge arrangement and authorization for a registration notice in the land registry, for approximately 700mila franchi. On 2 dicembre 2015, the Council of State granted the withdrawal through a government resolution and indicated that it would entail a reduction in the pension entitlement. The amount had been reported by Corriere del Ticino on 8 maggio 2018.
During 2020, parliament amended the remuneration and pension provisions of members of the Executive. The resolution had reserved the right to review the calculation of the insurance period in the event of future rules. The questions now concern the reference annual salary, who calculated the pension entitlement Zali will receive starting on 1° ottobre, the percentage reduction linked to the 700mila franchi, and the effects of the amendment on the insurance period. ## What a cross-border worker can infer
### The source's practical limitation
For someone who is a cross-border worker and works in Ticino, the news has a precise scope. The text concerns Claudio Zali's pension and the operation of the pension scheme for members of the cantonal Executive. It does not present a change concerning the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, remittances or withholding tax. These topics are not linked to the interpellation.
This distinction is necessary to avoid automatically transposing the case into the everyday life of a commuter. The approximately 700 thousand francs mentioned in the interpellation are the amount of the withdrawal requested by Zali and granted by the Council of State in the case described. The source does not present them as a parameter for a payslip or for the contributions of a cross-border worker. Nor does it provide a final value for the pension, an already calculated percentage or a reference annual salary: these are precisely some of the points on which Sergi and Pronzini are asking for an answer.
The text nevertheless makes it possible to distinguish three aspects. The first is the pension position accrued in the transition from the Appeals Court to the Council of State. The second is the effect that Ipct's internal opinion and the resolution of 2 December 2015 attributed to the early withdrawal. The third is the possible consequence of the 2020 parliamentary amendment on the calculation of the insurance period. The interpellation does not say that these three aspects have already been brought together in a definitive calculation.
For the cross-border reader, the question to keep in mind is therefore which information is documented and which remains to be clarified. The source documents the existence of the political request and reconstructs the cited acts; it does not document a new rule for those who cross the border. To navigate the separate topics of Permesso G/B and AVS/LPP e rendita, it is better not to use this case as a substitute for a specific guide. The topic of withholding tax is also not addressed by the article.
The most prudent reading is this: the case concerns an individual position held by a State Councillor, the rules applicable to that role and the questions addressed to the government. As long as the available material does not include the calculation, the response to the questions and the exact effects of the 2020 reform, any further conclusion about the pension treatment of a cross-border worker would remain outside the source.

### Four steps based on the cited documents
1. Start with the subject of the interpellation. The questions are addressed to the Council of State and concern the reference annual salary, the party that calculated the pension starting from 1° ottobre, the percentage reduction linked to the withdrawal of 700mila franchi, and the effect of the change in the calculation of the insurance period.
2. Keep the 2015 documents distinct. The internal Ipct opinion appears on 28 settembre 2015; Zali's question is dated 27 novembre 2015; the government resolution arrives on 2 dicembre 2015. This sequence makes it possible not to confuse the opinion with the decision.
3. Separate the judicial step from the administrative part. The order not to proceed of 6 marzo 2019 concerns the matter of the early withdrawal and bears the signature of public prosecutor Andrea Pagani. The source cites it as the starting point of the interpellation, not as a response to the four current questions.
4. Verify the point left open since 2020. Parliament changed the remuneration and pension provision of Executive members; the 2015 resolution had reserved the right to review and amend the calculation of the insurance period in the event of new rules. The interpellation asks what effect that change had on Zali's pension. The text provided does not report the government's response.
For a cross-border reader, this is a reading procedure, not a form to fill out. The source does not indicate documents to submit, offices to contact, or a deadline for sending personal questions. It does, however, indicate the names of the acts and institutions that make up the matter: Ipct, Council of State, parliament, Court of Appeal and public prosecutor. These are the coordinates not to mix up when trying to understand whether a figure concerns a withdrawal, a reduction in the pension or the calculation of the years.
It is not possible to derive from this reconstruction a calculation for one's own payslip, nor an answer about pension provision or withholding tax. item.title: Varese-Season 1-1: Manganese for 95'rigour
item.description: Varese snatches a point from Lentigione thanks to Mangano’s decisive save in stoppage time, after Beretta’s goal and Bontempi’s equalizer.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Beretta puts Varese ahead in the 4th minute - Bontempi equalizes in the 40th minute of the second half - Mangano saves Nappo's penalty in stoppage time - Varese-Lentigione ends 1-1
## Key facts - Match → Varese-Lentigione 1-1 - Lead → Beretta in the 4th minute of the first half - Equalizer → Bontempi in the 40th minute of the second half - Decisive save → Mangano saves Nappo's penalty - Stadium → Franco Ossola - Next fixture → Crema - Coppa Italia → Pro Patria at Masnago on Wednesday 7 October
### A point defended in stoppage time In the 4th minute of the first half, Varese broke the deadlock against Lentigione. Beretta exchanged passes with Favale, entered the box and beat Mosca with an inside-foot touch that went in at the far post. The goal put the biancorossi 1-0 up after a strong start. Varese's defense held firm and the lead stood without much trouble, although Varese's attack failed to make an impact.
The match remained 1-0 to the biancorossi until the end of the second half. The visitors, who played almost entirely in Varese's half in the second half, increased the pressure and in the 40th minute found space for the equalizer. Jassey crossed from the right, Bontempi was left unmarked in the box and headed in the 1-1.
After the goal, Lentigione continued to push. Almost as the five minutes of stoppage time were about to expire, another turning point came: the referee awarded the Emilian side a penalty for Bruzzone pulling Bontempi. Nappo took it, but Mangano guessed the side and saved the shot. The penalty duel was thus won by the Varese goalkeeper, who preserved the 1-1 and allowed the team to take at least a point.
The result moves the team up the table, but cannot make the Franco Ossola happy, as it had hoped to celebrate the season's first home win. Varese had the lead, defended it for a long time and then risked losing it late on. Mangano's save prevented Lentigione's comeback and secured the draw, leaving the biancorossi with a point after a second half considered too passive. ## The match setup
### The initial choices The return to the Franco Ossola came after Varese had broken the duck at Pontedera with their first league win. The Biancorossi were therefore looking to give their fans the season's first home joy. However, a far-from-soft Lentigione arrived at Masnago, a team aiming for a high finish in the table and coming off three consecutive wins before being beaten 1-0 at home by Cittadella Modena.
Ciceri set Varese up in a 4-3-3, dropping De Ponti back into defense to make room for Piantoni in midfield alongside Malinverno and Beretta. Favale, Barzotti and Bianchi started up front. Lentigione chose the same formation. Pedrelli, suspended, was replaced on the bench by Costa; in midfield the visitors fielded former player Battistello, while Mascanzoni, with Jassey and Alessandrini, led the attacking line.
### The first-half chances The opening minutes were a feeling-out period, until the first Biancorossi attack. In the 6th minute, Varese tried to double their lead, but Favale struck a poor shot from outside the box after a fine move. Lentigione took a few minutes to make their presence felt, and Mangano was immediately alert to Battistello's through ball for Mascanzoni. In the 13th minute, the goalkeeper came off his line low to stop Alessandrini, played through vertically by Mascanzoni.
Ciceri's side continued to keep danger at bay thanks to high, organized pressing, which allowed them to win back possession well away from Mangano's goal. The match remained without any major chances until the 25th minute, when the referee awarded Lentigione an indirect free kick inside the box. The move had originated from a back pass by Salera, clearly deflected by an opposing attacker, which Mangano had then caught with his hands.
The decision prompted protests from Varese and Ciceri's disapproval. Nappo, however, fired over, prompting a sigh of relief at the Franco Ossola. In the 34th minute, the Emilian side created their real chance of the first half with a ground-based move involving all three attackers: Mascanzoni finished centrally and Mangano parried.
Late in the half, Lentigione tried to push forward with greater intensity. Varese dropped back a few yards, without allowing themselves to be pinned back, and also held firm against the visitors' corners. The Biancorossi side thus reached halftime still maintaining their lead. ## The follow-up between Crema and the Coppa Italia
### The next appointment Next week, Varese will be playing in Crema. The away match is seen as an opportunity to seek another positive result and find the necessary momentum ahead of the next commitment. In fact, on Wednesday, October 7th, Pro Patria will arrive at Masnago for the Coppa Italia challenge.
The course of events is therefore already outlined: first the match in Crema, then the home match against Pro Patria. For Varese, these will be the next two scheduled appointments following the draw with Lentigione, with the search for a positive result and the cup match set in Masnago.

item.title: Trofeo Binda: appointment on March 14, 2027
item.description: Cittiglio confirms itself as the capital of women's cycling: 14 marzo 2027 sees the return of the Trofeo Binda WorldTour and the junior event in the Valli del Verbano.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- The Trofeo Binda returns on Sunday, 14 March 2027. - Cittiglio hosts the Trofeo and the junior race. - The starting location will be unveiled on 16 October. - The two races will finish in Alfredo Binda's hometown.
## Key facts
- Main race → Trofeo Alfredo Binda – Comune di Cittiglio - Junior race → Piccolo Trofeo Alfredo Binda – Valli del Verbano - Date → Sunday, 14 March 2027 - Circuit → UCI Women's WorldTour - Starting announcement → 16 October, at the headquarters of the Comunità Montana Valli del Verbano
### Confirmation for 2027
On Sunday, 14 March 2027, Cittiglio will once again be at the heart of women's cycling with a day built around two competitions. The programme will bring together the Trofeo Alfredo Binda – Comune di Cittiglio, an UCI Women's WorldTour event, and the Piccolo Trofeo Alfredo Binda – Valli del Verbano, reserved for junior women.
The format includes two separate moments on the same day. In the morning, the young riders of the Piccolo Trofeo will race, while in the afternoon it will be the turn of the WorldTour champions. For both races, the finish will be in Cittiglio, Alfredo Binda's hometown. This is where the entire event announced by the Valli del Verbano will conclude.
The announcement about the next edition comes as the Road World Championships are taking place in Montréal. The return of the international classic and the junior race is therefore already set for the date indicated, with Cittiglio once again at the centre of the day dedicated to women's competitions.
The double event brings together different levels of women's cycling: on one hand, the competition reserved for juniors, and on the other, the race included in the UCI Women's WorldTour international circuit. The two races are presented as a single sporting event, with the morning dedicated to the young riders and the afternoon to the elite athletes.
The next edition will therefore not be just one race, but a day structured around two competitions with the same finish. The first piece of information made public is the date; the starting location will be announced at a later time, at the event already scheduled for October. ## The results from Montréal
The announcement of the date is accompanied by two world medals that strengthen the connection between the Cittiglio race and international cycling. The results came during the Road World Championships held in Montréal and concern both categories highlighted by the Binda event.
Matilde Rossignoli, who won the Piccolo Trofeo Binda in Cittiglio last March, won the silver medal in the junior world championship event in Montréal. The young athlete's result directly connects the race reserved for juniors with the world stage: the winner of the last edition mentioned reached the podium in the world championship competition in the same category.
Among the elite, Elisa Longo Borghini won bronze. The cyclist had already won Binda in 2013 and 2021, two previous victories mentioned alongside the new result achieved in Canada. The two medals thus accompany confirmation of the next event and highlight the relationship between the Cittiglio competition and the world championships.
| Athlete | Result in Montréal | Link with Binda | |---|---|---| | Matilde Rossignoli | Silver in the junior world championship event | Winner of the Piccolo Trofeo in Cittiglio last March | | Elisa Longo Borghini | Bronze among the elite | Winner of Binda in 2013 and 2021 |
### The organization's work
From Montréal, Mario Minervino, president of Cycling Sport Promotion, explained that work on the 2027 edition has already begun. His statement reflects the desire to once again create a great day of women's cycling together with the institutions, communities and all the people who support the organization.
> «We have already begun working on the 2027 edition – Mario Minervino, president of Cycling Sport Promotion, explains from Montréal –. Once again, we want to create a great day of women's cycling together with the institutions, communities and everyone who supports us».
During his stay in Canada for the World Championships, Minervino also met with David Lappartient, president of the UCI. The results of Rossignoli and Longo Borghini, the words of the president of Cycling Sport Promotion and the meeting with the head of the UCI accompany confirmation of the new edition of the Trofeo Binda. ## The next event is on 16 ottobre
The first step toward the 2027 edition is scheduled for 16 ottobre at the headquarters of the Comunità Montana Valli del Verbano. On that occasion, the starting location of the two competitions will be announced, completing the first information made public about the next event in Cittiglio.
The announcement will cover both the Trofeo Alfredo Binda – Comune di Cittiglio and the Piccolo Trofeo Alfredo Binda – Valli del Verbano. It is therefore not the presentation of a single race: the location announced will be the starting point for the two races scheduled for Sunday 14 marzo 2027.
### The venue for the announcement
President Simone Castoldi will host the event. The headquarters of the Comunità Montana Valli del Verbano will thus host the moment when the starting point of the competitions will be revealed, while their finish is already set for Cittiglio, the birthplace of Alfredo Binda.
The schedule of the next stages is already defined. The start will be announced on 16 ottobre; 14 marzo 2027, meanwhile, will see the women's cycling day take place. The young riders of the Piccolo Trofeo will be the protagonists in the morning race, while the WorldTour champions will race in the afternoon. The junior race and the one included in the UCI Women's WorldTour will therefore remain united in the same event, with two distinct moments and a shared finish in Cittiglio.
The October announcement represents the first step toward the new edition. The race date has been confirmed by the Valli del Verbano, while the starting location will be made public at the headquarters of the Comunità Montana. The countdown to Cittiglio has already begun.

### The disputed transfer
For the 2027/2028 school year, the Municipality of Como proposed a reorganization of the city's school network. The document, included in the debate on the reorganization sought by the administration of Mayor Alessandro Rapinese, indicates in points 4.4.4 and 4.4.5 the transfer of the Via Tomaso Perti school complex to IC Como Lago. The Nazario Sauro Primary School is located in the school complex, the school from which Ilaria Flauto's reflection originates.
Flauto writes in her dual capacity as a teacher at Nazario Sauro and as vice-principal and primary school coordinator for IC Como Borgovico. The assessment she submits to the editorial office is clear-cut: the choice, examined from a pedagogical and regulatory perspective, causes concern and dismay. In her reading, the issue concerns the way the school is viewed: not as a simple sum of numbers or as a school complex to be moved based on accounting or demographic needs, but as a community built over time.

The teacher refers to school legislation and the National Guidelines. The Comprehensive Institute, she explains, was created to ensure vertical teaching and educational continuity, from ages three to fourteen. A unified pathway should therefore bring together a cultural, methodological, and social identity rooted in the local area.
Nazario Sauro had already changed institutes in 2016, moving from IC Como Centro Città to IC Como Borgovico. Since then, according to the letter, the teachers' work has built a cohesive and integrated educational community. The phrase Flauto chose to describe this transfer is direct: «In these ten years, we have not been a postal package».

The results mentioned include a shared horizontal and vertical curriculum, continuous teacher training, joint projects in music, sports, art, and language, as well as the design of educational spaces funded by the PNRR.

For Flauto, removing Nazario Sauro from IC Como Borgovico would change its identity, also because the institute is set to be renamed IC Como Nord Ovest and would lose its historic primary school in the city center. item.description: 54% of voters rejected the 19,1-million plan to enhance and modernize the UNESCO site of the Bellinzona castles; turnout at 47,5%.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Bellinzona rejected the «fortress» project - The no vote reached 54% of the votes - The plan provided for 19.1 million francs - Voter turnout was 47.5%
## Key facts - Outcome → 54% opposed and 46% in favor - Turnout → 47.5% - Investment → 19.1 million francs - City's share → approximately 4.5 million francs - Objective → enhancement and modernization of the UNESCO site
### The result in Bellinzona The vote by Bellinzona's citizens halted the project called «fortress», supported by the municipal executive, the City Council and the civic committee «Facciamoci Belli». Opponents obtained 54%, while supporters stopped at 46%. Voter turnout was 47.5%.
The proposal concerned the enhancement of Bellinzona's castles and aimed to relaunch and modernize the UNESCO site. The total planned investment amounted to 19.1 million francs. The plan was largely supported by the Canton, the Confederation and private parties, with a share of approximately 4.5 million francs borne by the City.
The consultation came after intense debate, a signature-gathering campaign and the subsequent popular vote. The result therefore concerns a project already supported by the municipal executive, the City Council and the civic committee in favor, but rejected by the majority of voters. The consultation figures combine the political outcome and turnout: the no vote prevailed with 54%, supporters garnered 46% and turnout was 47.5%.
The plan submitted to citizens had a precise financial scope and a defined objective. On the one hand, it provided for an investment of 19.1 million francs, with approximately 4.5 million francs borne by the City. On the other, it had been conceived to give new impetus to the UNESCO site of the castles through enhancement and modernization. The project therefore linked the enhancement of the castles to an investment supported by multiple parties, involving the City, the Canton, the Confederation and private parties. The vote rejected the proposal supported by the civic bodies in favor. ## The debate on the project
### The opposing committee The vote took place after a heated discussion around the proposal’s approach. The project had been at the center of a broad debate, which had first led to the collection of signatures and then to the popular vote. The opposition mobilization had a precise structure: the committee was mainly associated with Noce and was led by former mayor Brenno Martignoni-Polti.
Avanti con Ticino&Lavoro, Partito comunista, HelvEthica and the Movimento per il socialismo had taken sides in support of that position. The front also included various prominent figures, among them democentrist deputy Tuto Rossi and architect Cristiana Storelli. The campaign against the project thus brought together a local committee, political forces and figures who had intervened in the debate on the enhancement of the castles.
### Costs, management and access The objections did not concern just one element. Among the points contested were the project’s costs and the management model envisaged for enhancing the castles. The opposing committee had also challenged the designation «Fortress», considered to be at the expense of the term «castles».
Another issue was paid access to the inner courtyard of Castelgrande and the Murata gallery. The discussion therefore concerned the cost of the operation, the organization of management, the name under which to present the complex and the methods of access to specific places.
The transition from the collection of signatures to the popular vote brought these points to the attention of the citizens of Bellinzona. The final result rejected the project supported by the proponents, but the objections described concerned costs, management, designation and paid access. The local debate focused on the costs and on how to manage and designate the complex, as well as on access to the inner courtyard of Castelgrande and the Murata gallery. ### The next step with the Canton Asked by RSI, mayor Mario Branda admitted his disappointment with the outcome of the vote. His reaction starts from the work already carried out: he recalled that the project had been in the works for a long time and had required a financial and human investment.
> «The project had been in the works for a long time: there was a financial and human investment.»
Branda explained that the rejection poses an obstacle, but does not compromise the project on which hopes had been placed to give Bellinzona fresh impetus from an economic, tourism and cultural standpoint. The mayor's reaction therefore combines disappointment over the vote with the possibility of considering how to proceed with the proposal.
The mayor recalled that the castles are owned by the Canton. He also stressed that the project had been sponsored by the City and the Canton. For this reason, after the vote, he indicated the need for contact with the cantonal authorities: the discussion will have to serve to understand what they think and what can be done now.
Branda specified that what happens next will not be such a foregone conclusion. The indicated step therefore remains linked to discussions between the City and the cantonal authorities, which own the castles and were involved in sponsoring the project. The result of the vote has opened this phase of dialogue following the public rejection.
In the same reaction, Branda admitted that the Municipal Council and those in favor had not been sufficiently effective in explaining the project. This is the self-criticism expressed by the mayor regarding the promoters' communication. The indicated next step remains contact with the cantonal authorities and an assessment of the possibilities following the rejection expressed by the citizens.

item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Welcome Celebration at Pedotti Primary School in Luvinate - Workshops on safety, prevention and first aid - State Scientific Police and Red Cross with the pupils - English, cyberbullying and school safety in the classroom

Pedotti Primary School in Luvinate devoted a morning to the Welcome Celebration. There was no traditional lesson for the children: the programme offered experiential activities and numerous workshops coordinated by the Teaching Staff, with safety and prevention as the common thread.
On Saturday, experts, professionals, volunteers and parents gathered at the school to describe and explain their activities to the pupils.
### Activities for the pupils
The most significant presence was that of the State Scientific Police. The officers illustrated evidence-gathering activities, using fingerprints, microscopes and special equipment. The demonstration brought tools and procedures related to the work of the Scientific Police into the school.
Alongside the Scientific Police, numerous Red Cross volunteers also took part. With the pupils, they covered the basic rules of First Aid and how to ask for help effectively. The workshop thus added the topics of intervention and requesting assistance to the programme.
Other activities included recognizing and defending against cyberbullying, useful English words for asking for help in a large city, and actions for a safe school. This last activity was linked to educating aware and active citizens. The morning thus brought together different experiences, all included in the programme of the Welcome Celebration. ## A network of experiences within the school
### Themes and contributions
The Welcome Festival did not focus on a single workshop. The organizers created a structured morning in which children and adults were able to approach different skills united by the themes of safety and prevention.
The contribution of the Red Cross concerned the basic rules of first aid and how to ask for help effectively. The State Scientific Police, on the other hand, demonstrated the work of searching for evidence through fingerprints, microscopes and special equipment. Alongside these activities, the program included cyberbullying, English for asking for help in a big city and actions for a safe school.
The cyberbullying workshop was dedicated to recognizing and defending oneself against this phenomenon. The English activity had a practical purpose indicated in the program: learning useful words for asking for help in a big city. The safe-school program, on the other hand, aimed to make students aware and active citizens.
Other activities took place to complete the week. The Carabinieri, the Intermunicipal Civil Protection Service and the Local Police had already come to the school for other learning experiences. The source presents these events as part of the same commitment to safety and prevention.
The work involved the Teaching Staff together with experts, professionals, volunteers and parents. The school therefore hosted different contributions, keeping the workshops within a single program dedicated to the students. Searching for evidence, first aid, cyberbullying, the English language and behaviors for a safe school were the topics proposed during the week and throughout the morning. ## Families and school together
### The role of the Parents' Association
During the morning and then at lunchtime, the Luvinate Parents' Association, as usual, organized moments of meeting and conviviality with families and parents. Its involvement accompanied the day dedicated to workshops with a space aimed at family participation.
Lunch and the meetings completed a Welcoming Celebration built around the school. The experiential component, coordinated by the Teaching Staff, was joined by the moments of sharing organized by the association. The presence of parents and families was already planned among the contributions of the morning, together with those of experts and professionals.
The Pedotti Primary School chose this path to launch the school year. The program brought the community, families and school together through activities on safety and prevention. The source describes this choice as the beginning of a new great alliance among these parties.
During the week, meetings with the Carabinieri, the Intermunicipal Civil Protection Service and the Local Police had prepared other opportunities for learning. The Welcoming Celebration then brought the State Scientific Police, the Red Cross, experts, parents and the Teaching Staff together at the school.
The program did not include a morning of traditional lessons, but experiential activities aimed at primary school children. The closing with the moments of meeting and lunch kept families and parents at the center, while the workshops addressed first aid, asking for help, cyberbullying, English and actions for a safe school.
The final thanks went to the Luvinate Parents' Association, which organized the welcome and conviviality. For Pedotti, the start of the school year was thus linked to collaboration among school, families and community.
